open_points.subject: flow:deliver_one_photo atomic-write failure cleanup
open_points.text: A failed atomic write removes its temporary file, unless that removal fails too; the temporary file then stays, as A6 rule 3 decides.
open_points.question: Must an ordinary failed image or record write attempt to remove its temporary file, or was that cleanup guarantee removed with the former A6 rule 3?
options: Every non-crash failure attempts removal; the temporary file remains only if removal also fails.
Atomicity protects only the destination; an ordinary failed write may leave its temporary file.
Temporary files may remain only when a crash cuts the write short.
open_points.default_guess: Retain the explicit flow behavior: attempt removal after every non-crash failure and leave the temporary file only if removal fails.

witness.initial: The binary-store or state destination is unchanged, and a write has created a temporary file but has not renamed it.
events: module:delivery_store encounters a non-crash write failure before the rename.
A cleanup-based implementation removes the temporary file.
An implementation following the revised A6 rule 3 leaves the temporary file because that rule specifies leftovers only for crash-cut writes and no longer requires cleanup after an ordinary failure.
outcomes: The destination remains unchanged and no temporary file remains.
The destination remains unchanged but a file whose name begins with TEMPORARY_NAME_PREFIX remains.
witness.observer: The installer or operator inspecting the binary store or state folder sees the difference.
